subject: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben@peopleops-consult.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, Acme Bio is moving to extend offers next week and wants our recommendation on two items they asked us to validate:

1) Title concordance across peers — they shared a handful of competitor job titles that don't map cleanly to our leveling (senior vs lead vs staff).
2) A simple, auditable geo-index approach for offer anchors (US coastal vs midwest vs EU hubs).

Could you send a small sample set (5-8 roles) showing: current Redwood band anchors, proposed peer-title mapping, and a suggested geo multiplier table? Something concise that we can attach to the offer playbook.

If you have an internal memo or precedent for a geo-index we can reuse, that would be ideal. We just need something defensible for HR and their compensation committee.

Thanks — I attached Acme's role list in my mail earlier.

Ben
Ben Wallace
Senior Consultant, PeopleOps Consulting
ben@peopleops-consult.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Wallace <ben@peopleops-consult.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers

Ben —

Attaching a quick sample workbook (benchmark_sample_v1.xlsx) that maps 6 Acme roles to our levels and shows two geo-index options: one market-driven (percentile-based) and one simplified band-offset (flat multiplier by region). Key notes:

- Methodology: peer list uses public market comp (levels.fyi, LinkedIn insights) + anonymized offer data from last 12 months.
- Title mapping: where title ambiguity exists I included a recommended concordance plus a short rationale line. Example: "Senior Software Engineer (Acme) -> Redwood L4 Senior IC (justification: scope & IC ladder)."
- Geo index options:
  * Option A (percentile): compute 50th/75th percentiles per region and scale anchor to a global base. Good for precision but heavier to maintain.
  * Option B (index multiplier): simple multipliers — Coastal US: 1.12, Inland US: 1.00, Small markets: 0.92, EU hubs: 0.98. Easier to operationalize for fast offers.

Quick ask: Markus — can you scan the title mappings for anything you disagree with? Neha — if you get a sec, want your view on the multipliers (especially EU hub rate).

If this looks fine I'll convert Option B into a one-page memo we can hand to HR and the hiring managers.

Thanks,

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
People Partner, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: benchmark_sample_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers

Lauren — thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. Quick inline notes below.

> "Senior Software Engineer (Acme) -> Redwood L4 Senior IC"
Looks fine. For two roles where Acme uses "Lead" vs our "Staff", I think we should treat those as L5 (staff) for scope but pay to L4 anchor + L5 stretch for higher candidates. Otherwise we risk over-indexing.

> Option B multipliers: Coastal US 1.12, Inland US 1.00, Small markets 0.92, EU hubs 0.98
I agree with the simplicity. My only ask is: add a 'San Francisco premium' carve-out for critical senior hires (+3–5%) rather than baking into all Coastal US — keeps the table easier to explain to finance.

Operational question for Neha: will Legal/Finance be comfortable with the flat multiplier approach for offers >$250k TC? If not, we should route those high-comp roles into percentile calculations (Option A).

Happy to discuss on a short call if helpful.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Dir, Talent Strategy — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers

Folks —

Appreciate the workbook. I reviewed and converted Option B into a short proposal (attached PDF: geo_index_proposal.pdf) with the following recommended values and guardrails:

- Geo multipliers (applied to global base anchor):
  * San Francisco / NYC hubs: 1.15 (SF premium carved out here)
  * Other US coastal metros: 1.10
  * Inland US / national average: 1.00
  * Small US markets: 0.92
  * EU hubs (London, Berlin, Amsterdam): 0.97
  * APAC major hubs (note: not in scope for Acme but for future): 0.95

- Guardrails:
  * Any offer with estimated TC > $250k or candidate with competing offers should default to Option A (percentile review).
  * People Ops to log the chosen method (A or B) in the offer thread for auditability.
  * Title mapping exceptions (e.g., "Lead" used differently by a peer) must be documented with 1–2 sentence justification.

I ran a quick sensitivity check on the sample roles — the multiplier table keeps anchors within +/-6% of a percentile-based approach for mid-level roles, which is acceptable for speed. For senior/exec roles there is more variance, so the TC gating above is important.

Next steps I recommend:
- Lauren to finalize a one-page memo (Option B table + gating rules).
- Mark us up on two example offers (Acme role 3 and role 5) using both Option A and Option B for the compensation committee.
- Lauren to share the memo with Ben and Acme HR once internal approvals are done.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Total Rewards, Redwood Inference
Attachment: geo_index_proposal.pdf (2 pages)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peer title concordance + geo indexing for upcoming offers

Thanks everyone — this is a good, pragmatic approach and I support moving forward with Option B as the default and the gating rules Neha proposed. A few action items before we share externally:

- Lauren: please convert Option B table + gating rules into a one-page memo and include the two example offer calculations (Option A vs B) as appendices. Target EOD Monday 2026-09-07.
- Neha: prepare a one-slide summary for Finance that shows expected budget variance if we adopt the multipliers for the next hiring quarter.
- Markus: stay on standby to approve title mapping edge cases; we'll route exceptions to you.

Once we have the memo and finance slide I'll give the green light to share with Ben/Acme HR. If there are any objections from Legal or Finance after their review we'll reconvene quickly.

Nice work — concise and defensible.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
VP People Operations, Redwood Inference
